title: GPU capacity backstop and degrade-aware routing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During a sustained customer workload spike on 2025-02-16 we observed progressive GPU pool exhaustion in eu-west hosted clusters that caused long request queue build-up, increased tail latency, and repeated throttling of low-priority tenants. This ticket consolidates the post-incident follow-ups: implement a capacity backstop (rapid soft-evict + redirect), a degrade-aware routing policy that routes to compatible quantized/cheaper model variants when latency SLOs are at risk, and telemetry/automations to detect pre-exhaustion signatures earlier.
background_and_timeline:
- 2025-02-16 03:12 UTC: spike starts (traffic from a large customer bulk inference job).
- 2025-02-16 03:20 UTC: autoscaler did not prime quickly due to hysteresis and pod start time variance; queue depth grew.
- 2025-02-16 03:36 UTC: observed KV-cache contamination and increased memory pressure on some hosts which amplified latency variance.
- 2025-02-16 03:45 UTC: on-call enacted manual throttles for bursty tenants; mitigation reduced tail but several requests failed fast.
- 2025-02-16 05:00 UTC: traffic subsided and pool recovered after manual remediation and scale-up (~90 minutes total impact).
root_cause_analysis_summary: Primary: Autoscaler hysteresis + delayed priming under cross-tenant prefetch patterns causing simultaneously high admission and slow capacity provisioning. Secondary: KV cache pollution and suboptimal 'all-or-nothing' admission that magnified queue resonance. Operationally we lacked an automated backstop that could quickly reduce queue amplification by redirecting mid-queue requests to cheaper model variants or to dedicated capacity tiers.
decision_rationale: We considered only improving autoscaler aggressiveness, but that increases cost and risks oscillation. Instead we chose a hybrid approach: (1) a fast reactive "capacity backstop" that can soft-evict / reroute a small percentage of queued requests to compatible model fallbacks or dedicated pools, (2) degrade-aware routing that prefers lower-cost/quantized variants when predicted tail latency exceeds threshold, and (3) telemetry signals for early detection (cache churn, admission-to-scale delta, rising queued token ratio). This balances reliability, cost, and minimal user-visible quality degradation.
proposed_design_overview:
- Backstop controller: lightweight service that subscribes to pool-level metrics; when queue growth rate and percent-cache-miss exceed thresholds it issues 'soft-evict' for low-priority tenants and publishes redirect tokens to the router.
- Degrade-aware routing: router consults model compatibility matrix (model -> fallback variants) and route-to-fallback when estimated end-to-end latency breach probability > 60%.
- Admission smoothing: implement short-lived per-tenant dampening windows (5s) to prevent synchronized prefetch retries.
- KV cache partitioning experiment: isolate KV cache per-tenant buckets for heavy-prefetch customers as an opt-in configuration for Dedicated tier.
- Telemetry: add derived metrics: queued_token_ratio, scale_delta_seconds, kv_cache_eviction_rate, predicted_tail_risk. Alerts + dashboard + synthetic workload tests.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Risk: Redirecting to quantized variants can degrade output quality; acceptable for non-SLA workloads but must be opt-in or accompanied by quality guardrails.
- Tradeoff: Backstop soft-evict is slightly user-visible (delay or redirect). Prevent broad false positives by conservative thresholds and canary rollout.
- Operational cost: additional orchestration logic and telemetry storage; mitigated by targeted thresholds and retention policies.

acceptance_criteria: AC1: Backstop controller can be enabled by pool with feature flag and perform soft-evict for at least one low-priority tenant without breaking routing.
AC2: Router can route to a compatible fallback variant and include audit metadata (original model, fallback model, reason) in request logs.
AC3: New telemetry panels show queued_token_ratio and predicted_tail_risk; pager alerts fire when configured thresholds are breached in staging tests.
AC4: Integration tests validate that fallback selection is deterministic and that redirect tokens cannot be replayed across pools.
AC5: Canary rollout shows decreased tail latency during synthetic spikes with less than 5% of requests served by fallback variants for default tenants.
